bug.short_desc: Incorrect day-view of multi-day appointments

long_desc.thetext: When I create an appointment spanning multiple days and check the "spans hole day" marker, the appointments shows up on all days but the last two ones. For example, when I enter an "in holidays" appointment from 2005-05-12 to 2005-05-15, it is shown on top of the day-view only on the 12th and 13th of May.
Please check again with >= 0.8.0-2
The bug is still there, it can easily be reproduced in the online demo on  http://demo.open-xchange.org.
Additional comment: only the last day will not be shown, not the last two days.
*** Bug 375 has been marked as a duplicate of this bug. ***

After reviewing this, i guess this is not a bug.  I try to explain:  According to whole day events for one day the start and end times are for example:  05/25/05 12:00 AM until 05/26/05 12:00 AM  If you want to have a two day whole day event, the times should be  05/25/05 12:00 AM until 05/27/05 12:00 AM  and for three day events one should use   05/25/05 12:00 AM until 05/28/05 12:00 AM  And then everything works like expected and the events are shown correct in ever day and in every view. Hopefully (it is very hot today) this is correct, but i will resolve the bug anyway and one can correct me if i am wrong.  Anyway, i found one superfluous line of code by testing this out ;-)

I think it'll be hard to explain my users why they should enter 05/28/05, when  the 3-day appointment in fact lasts only until (and including) 05/27/05.  However, I've just tried this again on the demo server, and now it seems to  work correctly. Did you already apply a patch to this system (although the  release number in the HTML code suggests you didn't)?    THX,    Carsten
Nope, no patch. I did not change anything.  I try to explain it:   It is the 05/28/05 12 AM instead of the 05/27/05 11:59 PM - the timespan is exactly 24 hours, right ?

Right.        And I have to correct myself: It still doesn't work. A whole-day appointment   with 05/25/05 as start date and 05/27/05 isn't shown on the day view of   05/27/05.      Since "12:00 AM" seems to be set automatically for whole-day events, i guess  one simply   could ignore the time data when selecting a day view's 24h events from the   database.
Yes, clear for me ;)   Please see comment #5 for more information.  The appointment ends 05/27/05 12 AM which means it should never be visible if you select the 05/27/05 ...

You're right in that this is not a "bug" (i.e., unexpected behaviour) from a  programmer's point of view, so let's leave the RESOLVE flag as it is.    However, a user entering 05/27/05 as end date of a 24h appointment would  usually expect that this date counts for the appointment. Consequently, OX  should either a) enter 23:59 instead of 00:00 as end time of 24h appointments,  or b) leave 00:00 as default and just ignore the time information for 24h  appointments as suggested in comment #8.    Should I post this as a feature request in the forum for further discussion,  or will you anyway change OX's behaviour as suggested above with a future  release?
a) can not be used because of incompatibility with other clients ... b) could be used ... will think about it.
changing resolution to later. need a concept.
This one is realy important for me to be fixed. Normal behaviour would be that the end date is included in the appointment.  Best regards, Martin Eggens

bug.short_desc: power outage kills user accounts and resets mailadmin password

long_desc.thetext: This is a patched OX-5 server Create user accounts in mailadmin section, server works fine. If there is a power outage you lose all the user accounts and the mailadmin password is reset to default. You cannot recreate accounts with the same name as a lost account. This is replicable and happened by accident the first time, but upon testing is happens each time the is a power loss to the server.  This is a show-stopper for us rolling this out, it should be able to take a crash and not lose account and particularly not reset a default mailadmin account password.  I will give more detials as I search throught the Db and log files. Steve D

Additional information Accounts that have been created survive if the machine has been rebooted. New accounts created on the machine (and the machine has not been rebooted are lost) this looks like a data commit to disk time lapse.  Accounts created hours before are not committed to the disk. The power outage that brought this to our attention took place about 12 hours after we originally set the box up. Every account and even the mailadmin account must still have been held in memory as we lost them all (mailadmin was reset to default password).
You find additional information and a workaround in the maintenance portal (Knowlegde section). Please note that this is a SLES 9 bug and you can also contact SUSE/Novell for further information.
closing

bug.short_desc: Adding distribution list to BCC field adds first entry to "To" field

long_desc.thetext: If you add a distribution list to the "bcc" field in webmail, the first entry of the distribution list is added to the "to" field. This only happens when using the German frontend (DE), NOT with the english one.  Can be reproduced in the online Demo, too.
Also happens when adding to "CC" in German.  Found in 0.8.0-4, too.
Please can you give me a step-by-step describtion, as I'm not sure what you mean. Thanks.

Ok, here we go:  Open Webmail, klick "Neue Nachricht", klick "BCC", select a distribution list, klick "BCC" (or "CC"), an you will see that the first entry in the lower window shows "An:".  This is not happening when you use webmail in the english version.  HTH.
Tried this with Firefox at the german online demo and it works without any problems! Maybe a browser related issue. Which browser do you use?
Used Browsers:  Mozilla Firefox 1.0.4 / Debian 3.1 Mozilla Firefox 1.0.5 / Windows 2000 SP4 Internet Explorer 6.0 / Windows XP SP2 Mozilla Firefox 1.0.6 / Windows XP SP2  On 3 different OX sites.

I'm sorry, but I can't reproduce it neither on the demo machine nor on my dev machine. Used browsers:  Firefox 1.0.4 (SUSE 9.2) Konqueror 3.2.1 (SUSE 9.2) Opera 8.5 (SUSE 9.2) IE 6.0.2600 (Win XP SP1) Firefox 1.0.3 (Win XP SP1)

It's a problem with certains translation. Javascript search "To: name" in the list. If a conatct as "To" in is name, when you click on Cc, it's copy as Cc: conatct  and as To: contact (in French, To is "A", so we have the bug for nearly all  contacts).  The bug can be easyly correct in the javascript (you have to search "To:" in  the beginning of the lines, and not "To" anywhere in the line.  I can post the fix if you want.

You're right!  My first contact begins with "An" (Anja), so this is the reason for being in the wron field! Stefan, finally we found it: Wrong parsing! We have to search for "To:"/"An:"/"A:", etc. at the beginning of the line.  Christophe, thanks for that, yes, please post the fix. My customers will be happy about that.
Ok, that's true :-)
assigned
ok, fixed it. thanks for the report.

bug.short_desc: Unable to delete appointments from shared calendar

long_desc.thetext: We have a user account with a shared calendar that all users can view. Those users with additional rights are able to create and modify entries in this calendar, but are not able to delete entries from the calendar, even though their permissions allow them to delete.  The process appears to succeed, but when the view returns to the calendar, the appointment is still there.
Please provide a step by step instruction so that we can reproduce this.

I have just discovered the option: only_owner_can_delete_private_folder_appointments=true  I believe that this is why the apointment wasn't being deleted, but why did the user not get a message indicating the cause? Also, the option to give users permission to delete items should be disabled when this option is set, or some message given to the user who is sharing the folder.  Step by step:  1. Create a user (User C) whose calendar will be shared. 2. Log in as the user and share the calendar. Give at least one user (User A) Admin permission in all categories, and a second user (User B) Edit all entries and Delete all Entries permissions. 3. Have user B create a new entry in the shared calendar. 4. Try to delete the appointment as User A and as User B. Neither will be able to delete the new appointment, but they will not get any message to that effect. 5. Log in as User C and delete the appointment - the appointment will now be deleted.

Yes, you are right. With the option "only_owner_can_delete_private_folder_appointments" the shared folder owner is able to delete himself from the appointment participant list or the whole appointment if he is also the object owner. I have to check this and give also the users who have write permissions the "delete permission" or a message should be displayed.

UserA creates an appointment on UserC's calendar.  UserA cannot delete this appointment even though she created it.  I would think UserA should be able to delete if they created the appointment for UserC.  Thoughts?

The possibility to delete such an appointment is given by the folder permissions and parameters set in configuration files.  User A should be able to delete the appointment because he works on behalf of User A and User C has the permissions to delete the appointment.  I am going to fix this issue ASAP.
This should be fixed, we have to test it in all variations.

Bug verified fixed on OX5 Build 5080.  Steps done:  In OX Groupware as User C: 1.  Create a shared calendar and share it to User A and User B 2.  Rights of User A: admin in all categories 3.  Rights of User B: edit and delete all entries  In OX Groupware as User B: 4. Create a new entry in the shared calendar of User C. 5.  Try to delete the appointment set by User B.  In OX Groupware as User A: 6.  Try to delete the appointment set by User B.  In OX Groupware as User C: 7.  Try to delete the appointment set by User B.   Result was: Users A, B and C were able to delete the appointment created by User C

long_desc.thetext: After changing the IMAP server configuration using the Admin web interface (I wanted to change the quota warning from 90 to 80%), users began getting the following error when deleting an e-mail in the Webmail interface:  The current command did not succeed. bug.short_desc: Appointment reminders should be sent to all participants

long_desc.thetext: It looks like that Ox appointments (and tasks, and projects) send reminders to the event owner only, ignoring the participant lists. In my opinion, this logic contradicts to the purpose of a GROUPware suite.  The proposed solution:  in appointmentReminder function (MailReminder.java  line 134) we replace single:  appointmentReminderWorker(oid, m, n, con, p);  with the next cycle:  ResultSet rsall = nrs.getResultSet("select member_uid FROM prg_dates_members WHERE object_id = "+oid+""); while(rsall.next()) { String member = rsall.getString(1); ComfireLogger.log("DEBUG: notification for "+oid+" to "+member, ComfireLogger.DEBUG); appointmentReminderWorker(oid, member, n, con, p); }  Same in taskReminder and projectReminder. Looks like that it does what I want: ALL event members are reminded about the upcoming event same as the event owner, unconditionally.  I see also some unused (?) parameter "multi_notification" in source code; "grep -R multi_notification /usr/src/open-xchange-0.8.2-1/*" Is it planned to be used to control reminders to other participants?  Alexey
I want to be reminded 15 minutes before the event starts and you 60 minutes before. Another participant wants no reminder at all. A reminder is always user specific in our opinion.

I completely agree that it is good to have user-specific reminders - as an option. Actually, they are present because each participant can set his/her own appointment in his/her private calendar.  But the enforced group reminders is a more important feature in my opinion. When I create a group event, I may not hope that all participants will set their own reminders upon "New appointment created" mail notification. I, as the appointment "admin", must be able to create appropriate automatic reminders for them. And I see no such functionality in OX 0.8.2. Is it my oversight?  All this is even more relevant to tasks and projects. All task members must be warned automatically about task expiration events, etc, even if the task owner is out-of-office; the existing taskReminder code warns the task owner only.

Closing this bug. There are now several ways that a participant will be notified about an event:  * Invitation E-Mails * Popup Dialog at the groupware * Appearance of appointments of the next 2 weeks at the portal  The concept of user-specific reminder settings has been kept untouched.
Closing

Hi,  I'm the original reporter of ticket #2006112310001718 and I just found this report here.   The solution to add "LDAP_USER_NEXT_UID_SEARCH_BASE_DN=..." is not working - at least for me. When I add this option to "Ldap.properties" and restart everything uidNumber just starts counting from 1000 again.  Searching for the highest available uidNumber is by the way not the correct resolution for this problem. It is more difficult:  - On SLES9 SP3 there is a special configuration in LDAP for UIDs and GIDs, e.g. ou=ldapconfig,dc=example,dc=com. You find there "cn=userconfiguration" and "cn=groupconfiguration". Both have three attributes to specify ID ranges: suseMinUniqueId, suseMaxUniqueId and suseNextUniqueId.  - So if you add a new user/group with YaST2 it looks up this configuration takes the suseNextUniqueId and uses it as new UID/GID. suseNextUniqueId is incremented by one and written back to LDAP configuration tree.  - Samba OXtender adds computer accounts with "smbldap-useradd" (I can see this in rootdaemon.log) and - as it looks like - respects the configuration in "ou=ldapconfig". That means "smbldap-useradd" works like describe for YaST2 above.  - So the correct solution would be that OXadmin also looks up this configuration area like YaST2 does.  Let me explain why extending the search tree for uidNumber from "ou=people,dc=example,dc=com" to "dc=example,dc=com" - as suggested in the resultion with LDAP_USER_NEXT_UID_SEARCH_BASE_DN would (in my opinion) not work:  - You add three new users with OXadmin: uidNumber=1000, uidNumber=1001, uidNumber=1002. Fine :)  - suseNextUniqueId has the value "1000" - this is the original setting when you have just installed a clean SLES9 with SP3 and added no LDAP users or SMB computer accounts.  - Now you add a new computer account with Samba. It will get uidNumber=1000 and increment suseNextUniqueId. The next computer account will get uidNumber=1001 and so on.  Searching for the highest uidNumber and incrementing it makes no sense, when Samba OXtender uses "ldapconfig" as YaST2 does on SLES9.   Solution would be if eigther Samba OXtender also searches for the highest uidNumber in LDAP tree and increments it by on or that OXadmin also uses "ldapconfig."  Kind Regards, Eike Hoffmann

Hi again,  I forgot something: There is an workaround for this problem which I'm using currently (or customer needs to start urgently with the new Groupware system):  - Change configuration in "ou=ldapconfig,cn=userconfiguration" and "ou=ldapconfig,cn=userconfiguration" to a high range of UID/GID numbers, e.g. "suseMinUniqueId=10000, suseMaxUniqueId=30000, suseNextUniqueId=10000".  - YaST2 and Samba OXtender will then create user, group and computer accounts (= normal user accounts) according to "ldapconfig" in this high range.  - And OXadmin can create uidNumbers from 1000 to 9999 without any duplicates. (While searching in "ou=people, ..." for the highest know uidNumber and incrementing it).  So something like "sharing" the available ID range ;)  Not a clean solution, but it works.   Kind Regards, Eike Hoffmann

ok, finally found the problem and the solution.  jdk1.5 and ant 1.6 is a bad combination, as explained here (http://www.vocaro.com/trevor/blog/2007/01/08/how-to-use-saxon-with-ant/).  The root cause seems to be changes in Ant 1.6 in the way it try finds non core librairies in the system and the result can gives random result.  The XSLT problem appears because JDK1.5 has the xalan XSLT processor (XSLT 1.0) "built in" and due to the preceding problem, it's used against the OX stylesheet definition (XSLT 2.0)... instead of the provided saxon8.jar.  to resolve this issue, do the following when compiling open-xchange-gui:  - apply the provided  patch to open-xchange-gui/build.xml or add the "-Djavax.xml.transform.TransformerFactory=net.sf.saxon.TransformerFactoryImpl" to Ant command line option.  and  - force the CLASSPATH environnemental variable when running ANT:  CLASSPATH=/opt/open-xchange/lib/ ant -lib /opt/open-xchange/lib -Dlib.dir=/opt/open-xchange/lib/ deploy   as a side note, when running RHEL5 (beat2 at this time) a working package configuration is:  ant-1.6.5-2jpp.2 ant-apache-regexp-1.6.5-2jpp.2 ant-trax-1.6.5-2jpp.2 ant-nodeps-1.6.5-2jpp.2

(every system should have that ;-)  second, the 'GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ...' give right to the open-xchange database only on the '%' host (and that *exclude* connection explicitly to 'localhost'). this fails because the following calls to 'mysql' are done with '-h localhost' ans thus, access is denied.

Created attachment 1737 ask for a mysql password and grant privileges to localhost only  this patch assumes all connections will be done from "localhost"  more GRANT must be done if some components of OX will be hosted on different hosts.
Reassign to maintainer.

The % char is the wildcard in mysql and means every X with X == host in this case. At least for my mysql Versions I tried on several Debian derivates.  http://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.0/en/grant.html  [...]   To accommodate granting rights to users from arbitrary hosts, MySQL supports specifying the user  value in the form user_name@host_name. If a user_name or host_name value is legal as an unquoted identifier, you need not quote it. However, quotes are necessary to specify a user_name string containing special characters (such as ‘-’), or a host_name string containing special characters or wildcard characters (such as ‘%’); for example, 'test-user'@'test-hostname'. Quote the username and hostname separately.  You can specify wildcards in the hostname. For example, user_name@'%.loc.gov' applies to user_name for any host in the loc.gov domain, and user_name@'144.155.166.%' applies to user_name for any host in the 144.155.166 class C subnet.  The simple form user_name is a synonym for user_name@'%'.   [...]  The oxinstaller currently only works on a default, untouched version of mysql which does not require to enter a password for root when doing a local connect.  Extending the installer to allow to specify a password for user root is an enhancement.

It looks like not all versions of mysql 5.0, at least not on all different Linux systems behave the same. Yesterday evening I had to learn, that e.g. on OpenSUSE 10.2, unlike documented. mysql 5.0 does NOT accept the % char as a wildcard.  I'll change it to localhost, as this _seem_ to work on more different OS versions.
should be fixed meanwhile in HEAD

This has most certainly to do with race conditions in the sieve interface. I declared the setSieve method in OXImap as synchronized, linearizing all threads there (which will hurt performance, but only if many people are editing their vacation notices). This will get rid of some of the above mentioned problems.  The other half of the problem (weird displays of mailfilters differing from the ones in the file) happen when LDAP and Sieve are inconsistent. The Admin Daemon saves the sieve script both in the LDAP directory and the sieve daemon and with the race conditions these could differ. Usually you can repair that by setting the vacation notice again, overwriting the sieve script in both locations.

bug.short_desc: Provide servlet with InitParams to make integrating 3rd party servlets easier

long_desc.thetext: Some servlets prefer to configure themselves via init parameters that in a normal servlet container are  specified in the web.xml  This patch enhances the OX custom servlet container with a way to specify init parameters  in .properties files. The parameters can be specified  1) Generally for the servlet class  2) More specialized per servlet path  Consider the following entry in the servletmapping.properties:  /ajax/vacation:com.openexchange.ajax.VacationServlet  According to this patch the server would try to load  /opt/open-xchange/etc/groupware/servletConfig/com.openexchange.ajax.VacationServlet.properties and all .properties files it finds in /opt/open-xchange/etc/groupware/servletConfig/ajax/vacation/  with the latter properties overriding the first.  The first part of the path (/opt/open-xchange/etc/groupware/servletConfig) can be configured in the  ajp.properties under key "AJP_SERVLET_CONFIG_DIR"

this is one of my favorites :-) already saw that during the implementations.  we should have at least something like this:  a) the big 'Save' button is to download a selected backup, not to create one b) we should have at least 3 panel menu options:    - Create (to create a backup)    - Restore (to restore a backup)    - Delete (to delete a backup) c) We should have a new tab(?) to restore a backup from a file. or even better we put it to the panel, like we did it for the add attachment dialog in the normal gui.  for the next sp: we could also add a new tab for auto backup settings, like make backup each 'time period'. auto upload it to an external ftp server, or something else. we had something similar in comFire and maybe in ox5.

So a big "download" button would be different.  Create, Restore, Delete, Download, Upload(!) is the functionality we should  have in the first release. Tabs for file/ftp sounds nice. bug.short_desc: DHCP "Kill-Switch" in Admin GUI

long_desc.thetext: Scenario: Otto Normalo owns a Grocery store around the corner. He heard about the advanced collaboration opportunities of the brand-new Open-Xchange Server Express Edition, which is hell simple to install/maintain. So he buys the Live-CD and installs it on his new server. He uses a static IP Address because it is documentated as the preferred way. Otto has no other network managing services, like a DHCP Server running but he also does not have a clue what DHCP is. After some days of usage, he crawls the admin interface and finds the "DHCP" switch. Just because Otto is a curious guy, he activates it and clicks "Save". After that he can go home, because the Server loses his previous IP address and tries to configure via DHCP which will fail because no DHCP is available. -> Dead-lock.
*** Bug 7639 has been marked as a duplicate of this bug. ***

Change from static IP to DHCP:   Before the mechanism is changed from static IP to dynamic IP, the admin has to  confirm this. The message should be:   ============= begin ================ You have chosen DHCP to configure the network settings of this server. This  means the server will request new (unknown) network settings from a DHCP  server.  Case 1 - hostname: The user interface will reload itself in a few moments. In  case the DHCP server is configured properly, you will be able to login again.  Case 2 - IP: This means the user interface will be available under a new  (unknown) IP address.   Please continue only if you know how to find out the new network settings of  this server.                  [Continue] [Cancel]  [Cancel] is preselected to avoid that users accidentially hit [enter] ============= end ================   DHCP success or failure has to be checked. In case of failure the static IP  settings have to be restored and the admin has to get a short notice "Network  configuration over DHCP has failed. Static configuration has been restored.".
How to "preselect" a button in our hover-confirmation windows?
Our buttons cannot be triggered using [Enter]. So our goal to prevent the user  from accidentially submitting something is perfectly met. :-)
Fixed with next release.

"Case 1 - hostname: The user interface will reload itself in a few moments. In  case the DHCP server is configured properly, you will be able to login again."  Uhm, i suppose you meant that the DNS server is automatically instructed by the DHCP Server to update its database for the changed IP address. This case is very untypical for most network configurations. For me it reads like "If you have a good DHCP server, your DHCP server will update the DNS automaticly." which is nonsense because it needs much more effort. In most cases, the DNS will point to the wrong IP and the user cannot login. This must be made sure to avoid disappointments.
At least this helps some customers. The alternative would be to say: "IP  address is going to change. Good luck." which does not help anyone.
For me, this leads the customer to the assumption that nothing bad can happen if he accesses the admin gui via a domain name.

That is why I said "In case the DHCP server is configured properly". This  actually means, "in case your DHCP server takes care of your hostname  configuration (DNS)" but I did not want to go into technical details there.

Yep, but being too smatter when describing a complex operations will create the feeling of a non-critical operation which is the case here. If the user is expected to have no in-deep knowledge about technical stuff he will not understand what he is doing here. This leads to critical error-scenario (whole server unavailable) where the user thinks he has done all right and blames the software developer. Except from this, this is no DHCP specific case but a DHCP/DNS specific one and im am sure that 99% of the target customers do NOT have such a configuration. The DHCP Server is configured "properly" if he blows out IP-addresses and lease-times, talking to a DNS Server and auto-configuration of this i NOT a default DHCP configuration which is covered by "properly".

Except from this, the DHCP Server does not know the System before because it had a static IP address and will give it a random address from it's pool. This implies that the DHCP Server cannot tell the DNS what machine is mapped with the new IP address.

bug.short_desc: FQDN is replaced by a DHCP value after installation

long_desc.thetext: I reproduced this on two different VMWare machines:  1. Run a default installation and enter a valid FQDN at the point it is prompted 2. After installation, check the FQDN ($ hostname -f) -> I set qaoxee-mbraun.open-xchange.com as FQDN, but after installation, qaoxee-mbraun.netline.de is set. I suppose this value comes via DHCP. Severity "Critical" because of non-intended configuration change.

I already somehow fixed that.  During install the hostname dialog now shows the fqhn as given by dhcp (as long as the dhcp server did send a fqhn) and uses this name as prefilled value for the inputwindow.  That's all we can do.
Bug reopened.  This occurs again in 0.99.7

? Yes of course! When you choose DHCP and override the dhcp hostname, then dhcp will override it again. If you want a static hostname setup dhcp must not be used. If you want a different hostname, then your dhcp proposes, reconfigure your dhcp.  That's not a bug, that's fact.  When you press the break on the car, it stops, even if you press the accelerator at the same time.

I DID enter a custom FQDN Name and its getting overwritten by the DHCP settings. If no DHCP Service is available, the "Example" FQDN is only hostname. There is no way to set a custom FQDN at the current installer.
after a phonecall I found out, that the real issue is:  - starting install, wait, until dhcp detection is done - press back - assign static ip and hostname  still the dhcp hostname is used

To summarize the Problem (In Case Comment #0 was unclear): It seems that the whole configuration of the STATIC FQDN depends on a FQDN which is delivered DYNAMICLY via DHCP.  Comment #5 is correct. Another issue which may be provoked by this is: 1. Interrupt DHCP discovery 2. Enter a manual network configuration 3. Set a manual FQDN entry -> Note that the "Example" FQDN entry only holds the hostname, not the FQDN. For me, this is a note that something is hardcoded to the FQDN delivered by DHCP. So, no FQDN via DHCP -> no FQDN at all  4. Finish the setup 5. Check the hostname (hostname -f) -> only the HOSTNAME is shown, not a complete FQDN, not the value the user has entered at the installation.
workaround: /etc/amavis/conf.d/05-node_id  #chomp($myhostname = `hostname --fqdn`); $myhostname = 'hostname.fqdn.tld';  to set a valid fqdn for amavis that makes it possible to startup correctly

Fixed in the latest cvs. The problem is that the servlet calls addMemberstoGroup after each create. But the create call itself, sets the new created user automatically into the group 1. I've now implemented a check that the error isn't thrown if the group 1 (default group) is affected. But I think this should be handled by the GUI or the servlet later. One solution could be to set group 1 on the right side in the group tab automatically and don't transfer it to the servlet. I don't know if this is possible, but this would be a better solution to this problem, than the workaround I've implemented now.  Stefan: Could you please comment on that.  For this time I'm closing this one as fixed.

Fixing it in the GUI is not a solution. As soon as anybody else using the JSON interfaces you'll have the same problem. So it's a good idea to just ignore this group when creating a user as you add it anyway. You may also just remove it in the servlet, so it's not send to the RMI backend. Therefore I add Marcus to Cc.
Maybe Manuel can give some input here how to deal in best case with this.

i would fix this in the user json interface, because its the only interface which can create a user and put him directly in more than 1 group. so we must implemenet a check in the user servlet which checks the sent groups. if group "1" is sent, we remove it if the user did not sent any other "default group" in the user object.

This solution sounds good. But there is one thing to mention. The default group mustn't be 1, so we need an external call through the RMI interface to find out which one is the default group. At the moment we have such a method only internally in the admin daemon but not in the RMI interface.

Note: My bug description is not correct. I said "All Groups And Users" which is always Group 0, but of course it should be "All Groups" :) But as Group 0 can't be changed it will be ignored by the GUI. Nothing which helps us to fix this problem, it's just to correct my description.

bug.short_desc: Delete Domain must check if domain used for mail

long_desc.thetext: 1. Login 2. create Doamin test2.net 3. create a user (u2) with email u2@test2.net 4. delete the domain test2.net 5. now you can't send user u2 mails!

This is normal severity, because:  http://www.open-xchange.org/cgi-bin/bugzilla/queryhelp.cgi#severity  # Blocker - Blocks development and/or testing work. # Critical - Crashes, loss of data, severe memory leak. # Major - Major loss of function.
Yes you are right, the bug is Major (Major loss of function)!  Because, the user is not more able to get emails!!!
sorry, i was to fast, set it as normal back  PS: perhaps ask pm what a bug this is?

When the admin deletes a domain, then he should expect, that email to this domain does not work, do you agree?  When I destroy my car, it does not drive, agree?  What is missing, is a popup: if you destroy your car, it does not work anymore.  I don't see this as a major bug, but I'll add pm to cc.  We need to add all kinds of such checks, sure, but that's not major.

We should not solve this in the server but in the GUI. When a domain is deleted  AND there are mail addresses using this domain, a short warning should pop up.  ----------------------------------------------- | You are about to delete the domain $domain. | | Unfortunately, there are mail addresses     | | using this domain. If you continue, some    | | users will not be able to receive mails.    | | What do you want to do?                     | |                                             | |                    [Continue] [Cancel]      | -----------------------------------------------  When the user clicks [Continue] the domain is deleted.

To avoid that GUI has to check all mail addresses and aliases, we keep the text  more general:  ----------------------------------------------- | You are about to delete the domain $domain. | | There might be mail addresses and aliases   | | using this domain. If you continue, those   | | will be deleted as well.                    | | What do you want to do?                     | |                                             | |                    [Continue] [Cancel]      | -----------------------------------------------  GUI, please fix and then reassign to server/admin. Server/admin: Please check what happens when the domain is deleted: Do the  users' mail addresses remain untouched? Do they get usable when domain is added  again? What will happen?

After a small check it turned out that after deleting a domain all email  addresses remain in the system and nobody has a clue what the result of such an  undefined state is. Therefore, we must make sure that our system cannot be put  into such an undefined state:  Admin server must check if any address or alias is using the domain and if so  an exception must be thrown. An array of affected addresses and aliases should  be given in that exception so that the administrator can look these up an  delete those.   === Additional note: The function "delete domain and all addresses and aliases" is  nice to have but can lead to a situation in which users end up without any  functional mail address. To be discussed.

wtf? array in an exception?! the server will throw an exception with text that the domain is currently in use by some users and that the admin should first reorganize their aliases before he can delete the requested domain.

Mail marked as spam will be fed into SpamAssassin's Bayesian classifier.  page sa-learn(1):  INTRODUCTION TO BAYESIAN FILTERING        (Thanks to Michael Bell for this section!)         For a more lengthy description of how this works, go to http://www.paulgraham.com/ and        see "A Plan for Spam". It's reasonably readable, even if statistics make me break out in        hives.         The short semi-inaccurate version: Given training, a spam heuristics engine can take the        most "spammy" and "hammy" words and apply probabilistic analysis. Furthermore, once        given a basis for the analysis, the engine can continue to learn iteratively by applying        both the non-Bayesian and Bayesian rulesets together to create evolving "intelligence".         SpamAssassin 2.50 and later supports Bayesian spam analysis, in the form of the BAYES        rules. This is a new feature, quite powerful, and is disabled until enough messages have        been learnt.         The pros of Bayesian spam analysis:         Can greatly reduce false positives and false negatives.            It learns from your mail, so it is tailored to your unique e-mail flow.         Once it starts learning, it can continue to learn from SpamAssassin and improve over        time.         And the cons:         A decent number of messages are required before results are useful for ham/spam determi-        nation.        It's hard to explain why a message is or isn't marked as spam.            i.e.: a straightforward rule, that matches, say, "VIAGRA" is easy to understand. If            it generates a false positive or false negative, it is fairly easy to understand            why.             With Bayesian analysis, it's all probabilities - "because the past says it is likely            as this falls into a probabilistic distribution common to past spam in your sys-            tems". Tell that to your users!  Tell that to the client when he asks "what can I do            to change this". (By the way, the answer in this case is "use whitelisting".)         It will take disk space and memory.            The databases it maintains take quite a lot of resources to store and use.  GETTING STARTED        Still interested? Ok, here's the guidelines for getting this working.         First a high-level overview:         Build a significant sample of both ham and spam.            I suggest several thousand of each, placed in SPAM and HAM directories or mailboxes.            Yes, you MUST hand-sort this - otherwise the results won't be much better than Spa-            mAssassin on its own. Verify the spamminess/haminess of EVERY message.  You're urged            to avoid using a publicly available corpus (sample) - this must be taken from YOUR            mail server, if it is to be statistically useful.  Otherwise, the results may be            pretty skewed.         Use this tool to teach SpamAssassin about these samples, like so:                    sa-learn --spam /path/to/spam/folder                    sa-learn --ham /path/to/ham/folder                    ...             Let SpamAssassin proceed, learning stuff. When it finds ham and spam it will add the            "interesting tokens" to the database.         If you need SpamAssassin to forget about specific messages, use the --forget option.            This can be applied to either ham or spam that has run through the sa-learn pro-            cesses. It's a bit of a hammer, really, lowering the weighting of the specific            tokens in that message (only if that message has been processed before).         Learning from single messages uses a command like this:                    sa-learn --ham --no-sync mailmessage             This is handy for binding to a key in your mail user agent.  It's very fast, as all            the time-consuming stuff is deferred until you run with the "--sync" option.         Autolearning is enabled by default            If you don't have a corpus of mail saved to learn, you can let SpamAssassin automat-            ically learn the mail that you receive.  If you are autolearning from scratch, the            amount of mail you receive will determine how long until the BAYES_* rules are acti-            vated.  EFFECTIVE TRAINING        Learning filters require training to be effective.  If you don't train them, they won't        work.  In addition, you need to train them with new messages regularly to keep them        up-to-date, or their data will become stale and impact accuracy.         You need to train with both spam and ham mails.  One type of mail alone will not have        any effect.         Note that if your mail folders contain things like forwarded spam, discussions of spam-        catching rules, etc., this will cause trouble.  You should avoid scanning those messages        if possible.  (An easy way to do this is to move them aside, into a folder which is not        scanned.)         If the messages you are learning from have already been filtered through SpamAssassin,        the learner will compensate for this.  In effect, it learns what each message would look        like if you had run "spamassassin -d" over it in advance.         Another thing to be aware of, is that typically you should aim to train with at least        1000 messages of spam, and 1000 ham messages, if possible.  More is better, but anything        over about 5000 messages does not improve accuracy significantly in our tests.         Be careful that you train from the same source -- for example, if you train on old spam,        but new ham mail, then the classifier will think that a mail with an old date stamp is        likely to be spam.         It's also worth noting that training with a very small quantity of ham, will produce        atrocious results.  You should aim to train with at least the same amount (or more if        possible!) of ham data than spam.         On an on-going basis, it is best to keep training the filter to make sure it has fresh        data to work from.  There are various ways to do this:         1. Supervised learning            This means keeping a copy of all or most of your mail, separated into spam and ham            piles, and periodically re-training using those.  It produces the best results, but            requires more work from you, the user.             (An easy way to do this, by the way, is to create a new folder for 'deleted' mes-            sages, and instead of deleting them from other folders, simply move them in there            instead.  Then keep all spam in a separate folder and never delete it.  As long as            you remember to move misclassified mails into the correct folder set, it is easy            enough to keep up to date.)         2. Unsupervised learning from Bayesian classification            Another way to train is to chain the results of the Bayesian classifier back into            the training, so it reinforces its own decisions.  This is only safe if you then            retrain it based on any errors you discover.             SpamAssassin does not support this method, due to experimental results which            strongly indicate that it does not work well, and since Bayes is only one part of            the resulting score presented to the user (while Bayes may have made the wrong deci-            sion about a mail, it may have been overridden by another system).         3. Unsupervised learning from SpamAssassin rules            Also called 'auto-learning' in SpamAssassin.  Based on statistical analysis of the            SpamAssassin success rates, we can automatically train the Bayesian database with a            certain degree of confidence that our training data is accurate.             It should be supplemented with some supervised training in addition, if possible.             This is the default, but can be turned off by setting the SpamAssassin configuration            parameter "bayes_auto_learn" to 0.         4. Mistake-based training            This means training on a small number of mails, then only training on messages that            SpamAssassin classifies incorrectly.  This works, but it takes longer to get it            right than a full training session would.

JavaMail API throws a SendFailedException if anything went wrong during transport of a message through SMTP protocol.  Additionally, this exception class indicates to which recipient addresses the message could be sent successfully and to which not, but the reason differs (unknown address, error in SMTP protocol, etc...). Well, for me this looks like a bug because there is no information about the File System. For me, a file system is a logical layer that stores data to a storage device. This may be measured in what rene wrote like Total/Available/Used storage in a generic unit like megabytes or gigabytes. This informs the user about the state of the file system which can be ext2/ext3/ntfs/fat32 and so on.  As the current available diagrams only show the count of file descriptors (which are NOT coercible files on the harddrive) this led me to the result that the description of this module is not correct. If a user sees "Filesystem" or "Dateisystem" he expects information about the state of current disk usage, not only a in-deep system information about file descriptors.  File descriptors are: "In Unix-like systems, file descriptors can refer to files, directories, block or character devices (also called "special files"), sockets, FIFOs (also called named pipes), or unnamed pipes."

For OXEE we definitely need something which is clear to the users: This is  something like free/used disk space of open file handles etc. Filesystem  related stuff is quite useless as our target OXEE customer will not know  anything about filesystems.  So again: What information can we have?

bug.short_desc: No quota checking for infostore uploads

long_desc.thetext: In this test, a user tries to upload a huge amount of data. I've a OX:EE Server with about 8gb disk space. The user uploads a 7gb DVD image for example. The operating system and ox already allocates 1.4gig. While uploading the file a error is shown that no more disk space if left. It seems that there is no upload check at all about how many disk space can be allocated by infostore entries. These uploads are done by casual users that do not have any information how full the HDD is.  This leads to the following issues at the admin interface: - Unable to create new backup - Unable to create new user - No upload of previous backup possible - No logfiles are created any more  The administrator tries to reboot the machine because something does not work. - system shutdown hangs at mysql, manual restart is required  After restart the following issues occur: - clamav does not start - mysql does not start, therefore no authentification, no data available - login to any web interface throws 503  As this issue can be triggered by a normal user without knowing that he is doing something wrong, this is a blocker as it takes the whole server down. The administrator has no possibility to recover the system.   Client OS: Other  Client: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; U; Linux i686; en-US; rv:1.8.1.4) Gecko/20060601 Firefox/2.0.0.4 (Ubuntu-edgy)  Reproducible: Always  Steps to Reproduce: 1. Connect to the server infostore via webdav 2. Upload file(s) that are larger than the free space of the server 3. Reboot the server  Actual Results: Alles kaputt  Expected Results: Upload quota for user-accessible areas should be checked. At least, the system needs to have some space for basic operations like restoring backups, deleting users and so on.

This is indeed a problem.  First of all, groupware has to delete the uploaded file if the upload fails due to no disk space. This ensures that the disk space isn't used anymore after the failed upload.  AFAIR the was a bug that stated all quotas should be disabled for OX EE. Maybe we have to think a little bit about this decision.  I'm going to check why the upload file isn't deleted on failed upload, that causes other services to fail on reboot.
We need a possibility to modify settings depending on the underlying hardware, anyway. See bug 8437
This is a critical bug and not a blocker. This should be fixed ASAP after the launch.
Carsten, bug #8437 has nothing to do with this one.

bug.short_desc: imap backend Dovecot not supported

long_desc.thetext: As of today, the CVS snapshot doesn't support Dovecot as the imap server.  His BANNER is not recognised by OX-hyperion.   Client OS: Other  Client: Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; Konqueror/3.5; Linux) KHTML/3.5.7 (like Gecko) (Kubuntu)  Reproducible: Always  Steps to Reproduce: 1.install & configure OX-hyperion 2.install & configure dovecot 3.create a user in both dovecot & OX with the same password 4.cannot use the webmail.  Actual Results: why it should'nt be supported ?  Expected Results: functionnal webmail
Created attachment 2889 add Dovecot to the list of recognised imap server  add Dovecot to the list of recognised imap server
Created attachment 2890 failing imap conversation dump

Since Courier & Cyrus specific implementation in OX is only related to ACLs and Dovecot doesn't have them enabled using one of these two implementation should be ok.  but trying to drag & drop a mail between INBOX and a user folder threw: Error code: Internal error: UID EXPUNGE not supported (MAIL-0020,1032912452-34) in the Web GUI  Tracing the imap backend conversation it appears there is NO "UID EXPUNGE" command sent to the backend from OX.  Since this command is fully supported in Dovecot (1.0.0) and many fat clients (thunderbird, outlook, ...) are ok with it, the imap parser of OX is failing somewhere between the GUI and the backend.  I attach the dump of a failing conversation between OX and Dovecot.  20071008-143537-26371.in 20071008-143537-26371.out  are trigerring the above GUI command. (see http://bugs.open-xchange.com/cgi-bin/bugzilla/attachment.cgi?id=2890)
OX-hyperion tries to do the drag & drop using:  A2 LIST "" INBOX A3 SELECT INBOX A4 UID FETCH 3 (UID) A5 COPY 1 RDV A6 STORE 1 +FLAGS (\Deleted) A7 LOGOUT  but no trace of "UID EXPUNGE" ...
after the error the message seems duplicated (one in the destination, and one in the source folder).

it can be read for some minutes in the two folders but then after about 5 minutes, it's not available in the detail pane:  "Error code: Message(s) 22 could not be found in folder INBOX (MAIL-0029,365143633-19)"  but it's listed in the list view and can be selected.  looks like some kind of refresh problem.

For the drag & drop part, i've digging into the problem:  the "message move" functionnality of hyperion rely on the UIDPLUS capability (imapCaps.setUIDPlus(imapStore.hasCapability(IMAPCapabilities.CAP_UIDPLUS)); in src/com/openexchange/api2/MailInterfaceImpl.java.  forcing this to true and the whole drag & drop is working.  reading RFC2359, it specify that "UID EXPUNGE" command is parts of the UIDPLUS imap extension.  manually checking the CAPABILITY string of dovecot (as 1.0.5, latest) is NOT returning the UIDPLUS tag in this capabilities. despite the official doc states it's supported (at least for UID EXPUNGE).  The final solution was to add UIDPLUS via the "capability" directive of dovecot. This way the backend expose the support of UID EXPUNGE and hyperion behaves correctly.  For this part this is NOT a hyperion bug, but I left it open for the first patch submitted and the first problem.  ps: I will go upstream dovecot to ask for the reasoning behind this and add a comment here then.
Reassign to mail component developer.  This issue may be fixed in HEAD. We have to discuss this first.

Actually UIDPLUS is not announced in dovecot 1.0 capabilities because it is not fully supported (only form mbox storage), but the UID EXPUNGE may be supported supported.  UIDPLUS is supposed to be fully supported in dovecot 1.1 (in beta2 at this date).

Based on a very short conversation with Timo on dovecot's IRC channel, it appears that UID EXPUNGE is supported and safe on a maildir backend with dovecot 1.0  Is any other UIDPLUS command required by OX ?
grepping the code OX makes use of - UID COPY (src/com/openexchange/imap/command/CopyIMAPCommand.java/CopyIMAPCommand())  the last UIDPLUS command (from RFC) seems to be not used (but I may be wrong)

Commands used: UID EXPUNGE UID COPY UID STORE UID FETCH  Reponse Codes used: APPENDUID COPYUID  Moreover the UIDNOTSTICKY status must not be indeicated on a folder SELECT command since assigned UIDs must be persistent
Added several fallback actions in HEAD repos as suggested by corresponding RFC to perform alternative ways on missing UIDPLUS extension.
Dovecot is officially supported since some time now, closing this one and assuming that the problem is solved.

Bug verified fixed  * A more readable error message has been added. * The behavior of the Groupware is correct in this case: User A shared the folder with "edit own" permissions. By creating a new appointment at the shared folder of User A, the creator (User B) is not the owner of the appointment, the appointment is owned by User A because it is his private calendar. Therefor User B cannot edit the appointment. Setting "Edit Own" for shared private folder is not really useful, because every appointment added by another user will be created in-person of the owner of the folder. This concept is useful in a boss/secretary scenario where the secretary creates appointments "for" her boss, but she does not own the appointment. The "Edit Own" permission is useful for public folders where no "owner" of the folder exists.  Verified Products OX5 SP4 Update 1 Build 5655

The problem is not caused by the GUI but by a faulty dovecot imap server that does respond on a  A1 LSUB "INBOX" %  with a response not containing the flag "\HasChildren". And therefore the subscribed subfolders of the INBOX are gone. Reassign. Going to check how some normal mail clients deal with this problem and if we are able to workaround this dovecot bug.

According to the RFCs (like I would understand them) this is not directly a bug of dovecot, because the RFC does not declare this implementation as a MUST-HAVE. The response flag (\HasChildren) is meant to be an extension to the IMAP protocol.  Other mail clients deal with it in the following form (got from the IMAP traffic of a thunderbird / simulated via telnet to keep readeable):  Escape character is '^]'. * OK Dovecot ready. 10 LOGIN hugo.test@oxserver.de test 10 OK Logged in. 20 LSUB "" "*" * LSUB () "." "INBOX" * LSUB () "." "Trash" * LSUB () "." "INBOX.Gesendete Objekte" * LSUB () "." "INBOX.Papierkorb" * LSUB () "." "INBOX.Spam" * LSUB () "." "INBOX.Entw&APw-rfe" 20 OK Lsub completed. 30 LOGOUT * BYE Logging out 30 OK Logout completed. Connection closed by foreign host.

The string "Anhänger.txt" is encoded in a mail-safe manner using the algorithm specified in RFC 2047, Section 6.1. So, everything is alright with the encoding.   Unfortunately there's no common sense among email clients how to decode/encode header data and a few cannot deal with particular forms of that encoding. bug.short_desc: Participants can be added to appointments which have private flag

Man kann mit diesen Commands alle Ordner ausser der Inbox bearbeiten, man kann die Namen der Standardordner ändern, man kann aber keine anderen Ordner überschreiben, doppelt belegen oder ihren Zweck ändern. Weiterhin ist es nicht möglich über diese Commands die Lage der Ordner in der IMAP Hierarchie zu ändern.  Eine Inbox ist eine Inbox und kein "Sent" Ordner. Diese Konzeptänderung werde ich in unser Backlog aufnehmen, bei einem für den Normalanwender sinnvollen Usecase für diese Funktion sowie einer entsprechenden Priorität könnte die Erweiterung für die nächsten Releases in Betracht gezogen werden. Danke für den ausführlichen Report und die Hintergründe.

bug.short_desc: Cannot add participants or view team if 'access-edit-public-folder' flag is off

long_desc.thetext: If the 'access-edit-public-folder' flag is off (for example in the 'pim_plus' access combination or, in other access combinations, turning it manually off), the user cannot add participants (both internals and externals) when creating new appointments/tasks and the 'team' view is also disabled.  Steps to Reproduce: 1. create a new user with the 'pim_plus' access combination (or, create a user with one of 'groupware_plus', 'premium', 'all' combination and then manually change the 'access-edit-public-folder' to off) 2. login into OX and select the calendar module 3. create a new appointment  Actual Results: 1. the 'Team' View is disabled 2. the 'Add' and 'Add external' Participant are both disabled  Expected Results: The user should not be able to create new subfolders under the 'Public folders' as implied by the 'access-edit-public-folder' flag set to off, but it should be able to add participants and view teams

Currently we do not have any special permission for the groupware functionalities. Therefore they are determined by combining some other permissions: - freebusy = calendar && fullSharedFolder && fullPublicFolder - teamview = calendar && fullSharedFolder && fullPublicFolder - conflicthandling = calendar && fullSharedFolder && fullPublicFolder - participantsdialog = calendar && fullSharedFolder && fullPublicFolder  Reassign to product management for a decision what to do with this problem.

This works exactly as designed: "...for example in the 'pim_plus' ..."  The main differentiation between PIM and Full Groupware is, that no group appointments, no team view and no public folders are possible. So the described behavior is exactly what shall happen.  The flag "edit-public-folders" is an internal flag, which is not meant to be used as a single switch.  Please reassign to documentation to clarify that in documentation if not stated there.

We've implemented an additional CAPABILITY call right after the users login. It's checked in to snapshot and should be available at software.open-xchange.com tonight. Could you check if it works for you?
